subject.title: Codex turn fails with generic Telegram fallback when invalid image tool model is configured, leaving child agent orphaned on full stdout pipe

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed on unknown explicit image-generation model refs at config/startup time, or preserve runtime flexibility and improve only turn-time diagnostics?
rationale: The safest fix boundary crosses config compatibility, provider/model catalog policy, Telegram user-facing errors, and Codex process lifecycle cleanup, so automation should not choose the product behavior alone.

options.title: Preflight explicit refs
options.body: Reject unknown explicit image-generation provider/model refs during config validation or doctor with focused upgrade guidance.

options.title: Runtime diagnostic only
options.body: Keep custom model refs flexible but surface a stable Telegram error id and clear provider/model failure when execution rejects the model.

options.title: Live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a real Telegram/Codex turn proves the orphaned stdout/stderr pipe path on current main.

recommendation.title: Preflight explicit refs
recommendation.body: Reject unknown explicit image-generation provider/model refs during config validation or doctor with focused upgrade guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans model catalog policy and Codex app-server lifecycle, both areas with recent feature-history evidence from this owner.
